key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin combines weld simulation, AI surrogates, and robotic control to screen in-space welding conditions before experimental testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could help engineers evaluate welding settings and compensate for robot speed changes during on-orbit assembly and repair.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates predict weld responses.
Simulated UR5 welding uses proportional control to adjust power-source settings near a seam corner.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs in repeated five-fold cross-validation; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-only; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation are still needed.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
